subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: gControllerButtons(0x803445C8), sFlags(0x803445CC), and sPreviousFlags(0x803445D0)/lbl_803445D4(0x803445D4) are FIVE independently-linked 4-byte .sbss globals, not one struct -- but they sit contiguously, so a TU that declares `extern u64 gControllerButtons;` and does `gControllerButtons & smallConst` reads the SAME 8 bytes as `gControllerButtons`(hi word) + `sFlags`(lo word) combined, and compiles to the identical 5-instruction and/and/xor/xor/or 64-bit-nonzero-test dance MWCC emits for a genuine u64 variable. When target's retail source at a SPECIFIC call site instead named the adjacent symbol directly (`sFlags` or `lbl_803445D4`) for just the low word, target's relocation differs textually (`sFlags` vs `gControllerButtons+0x4`) even though both resolve to the SAME final address and both sides execute IDENTICAL semantics -- objdiff's relocation-address-aware fuzzy/exact scoring already treats these as a MATCH (proven 100% fuzzy on ClockOncePerFrame with this exact alias present); only fndiff.py's naive TEXT diff (`--count`/`--clean`) counts it as a mismatch. Do NOT attempt to rewrite the C expression to force the `sFlags`-named relocation: any expression that names `sFlags` and `gControllerButtons` SEPARATELY either (a) lets the optimizer prove the high-word AND is dead and collapse to a single 32-bit load+rlwinm (shorter than target, real gets WORSE), or (b) forces genuine 64-bit shift/OR construction that invokes a `__shl2i` runtime helper (longer than target, real gets WORSE) -- both forms verified negative. Leave `gControllerButtons & mask`/`gControllerButtons & mask` as-is; treat this specific alias mismatch as NON_TEXT-equivalent noise in `real`/`--clean`, not a genuine residual, when auditing a function's remaining gap.
